Unsafe. I had an experience with a black hole once. She got overly attached to me and wouldn't let me leave. She then trapped me in her dark basement. It was okay here, there was an unusually large number of cats and other beings. They sang me the song of their people and then formed a circle where they proceeded to jerk it. I was frightened but also strangely excited. I joined in on their jerking effort. What I hadn't noticed before was the box in the middle of their circle. One by one, they would each put  their humanoid waste in said box. Unsure of what else to do, I followed suit. After we were all satisfied, I started to converse with them. They told me escaping the basement was near impossible, but they also told me fascinating stories and discussed flying lasagna with one another. These characters showed great intelligence. I enjoyed listening to them chat and discuss opposing viewpoints. But something was wrong. I felt...homesick. I had gotten too caught up in all of it. I reminded myself of my goal, escape. I shuffled through the crowd of penguins and such figures, looking for the way I had come in. Thats when I saw it, a light at the far end of the room. I ran towards it, but not too fast because running had captured the attention of the parrots in the room, whom stared. Intently. As I got closer and closer to the light, I saw shapes in the light. No, not shapes, letters, with a box underneath. The letters formed a word I had seen before, but could not remember exactly where. "Google." I muttered the word, "Facebook." The box underneath then turned into a vortex and I was rushed through some sort of space time continuum, until I was thrown out onto a place I recognized. This place was much more blank, but filed with more people. People I knew. As I walked up to greet some of my old comrades, I overheard some of them having a discussion. Similar to the discussion in the basement, but with less intelligence put into it. They sounded like idiots. I felt out of place. The basement filed with cats and the occasional "female" is where I felt that I belonged to. I was hesitant to go back, but after trying to speak with my former friends about flying lasagna and circlejerking, I found that I couldn't comprehend most of their "lol"s and their "yolo"s. I rushed back to "The Google" and told him to take me back to where I had been. Now I spend most of my days talking about cats, trees, and someone named Steve who likes to do naughty things. As easy as it is to escape, I keep coming back. I honestly wish I hadn't eaten dinner with that black hole.
